security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, documentation links, placeholder API-key text, and local Redis configuration examples. One real risk remains: the guide includes destructive SQL and WP-CLI database maintenance commands without backup, staging, or confirmation safeguards. No prompt injection or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Destructive database cleanup examples lack safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: Add backup steps, staging validation, dry-run or select-only previews, and explicit confirmation before DELETE, OPTIMIZE, or WP-CLI deletion commands.

remediation.issue: API key examples place the key in command URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Show environment variables or ignored local config files for API keys, and warn that command history and logs may expose URL parameters.

remediation.issue: The Lighthouse example installs a global npm package.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer npx or project-local installs, and mention that package installs can run lifecycle scripts.

content.value_statement: Slow WordPress pages hurt search visibility and conversions. This skill guides Core Web Vitals fixes, caching, media compression, asset tuning, and speed testing.
actual_capabilities: Lists Core Web Vitals targets for LCP, INP, and CLS.
Recommends image formats, dimensions, compression plugins, and lazy loading settings.
Provides caching guidance for LiteSpeed, browser cache, Redis, and WordPress transients.
Shows asset optimization examples for CSS, JavaScript, fonts, and preload tags.
Includes database cleanup, CDN cache headers, and speed testing workflows.
limitations: It does not run live audits without user-provided site access or commands.
Database cleanup examples require backups and staging validation before production use.
Plugin and CDN recommendations must be adapted to each hosting stack.
API-based tests may require user-owned keys and external service limits.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow Pages
use_cases.description: Identify likely LCP, INP, CLS, media, caching, and script issues from site symptoms or audit results.

use_cases.title: Plan Performance Fixes
use_cases.description: Create an implementation plan for image optimization, caching, deferred assets, fonts, Redis, and CDN headers.

use_cases.title: Standardize Speed Reviews
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable checklist for launch reviews, maintenance audits, and performance monitoring across client sites.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Slow Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WordPress page performance symptoms: [URL or notes]. Identify likely Core Web Vitals issues and list fixes in priority order.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Media Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this media library summary: [sizes, formats, plugins]. Recommend image and video optimization steps for WordPress, including safe defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Caching and Assets
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WordPress stack: [theme, plugins, host, CDN, cache plugin]. Recommend caching, CSS, JavaScript, font, and Redis changes with risks.

prompt_templates.title: Build Speed Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a repeatable speed monitoring process using Lighthouse, PageSpeed Insights, or WebPageTest. Include thresholds, reporting cadence, and rollback triggers.

output_examples.input: A homepage has a 4.8 second LCP, large hero image, and no CDN.
output_examples.output: Priority plan: compress and convert the hero image, preload the LCP asset, enable page cache, add CDN image delivery, then rerun mobile Lighthouse.

output_examples.input: A WooCommerce site has slow admin pages and frequent database timeouts.
output_examples.output: Suggested review: check object cache readiness, inspect autoloaded options, limit revisions, clean expired transients safely, and validate every database change on staging.

output_examples.input: An agency needs a launch checklist for client WordPress sites.
output: Confirm Core Web Vitals targets and mobile Lighthouse baseline.
Verify image compression, lazy loading, caching, CDN, and font settings.
Document rollback steps for database, plugin, and cache changes.

best_practices: Run performance tests before and after each change using the same device profile.
Test cache, minification, and script deferral changes on staging before production.
Back up the database before cleanup commands or plugin configuration changes.
anti_patterns: Do not delete revisions, transients, or metadata on production without backups.
Do not combine or defer all scripts without checking checkout, forms, and animations.
Do not treat one Lighthouse score as proof of sustained real-user performance.

faq.question: Does this skill run speed tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Tests require user-approved commands, URLs, and any needed API keys.

faq.question: Can it help with Core Web Vitals?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains target values and gives practical fixes for LCP, INP, and CLS issues.

faq.question: Does it recommend WordPress plugins?
faq.answer: Yes. It mentions image optimization, caching, Redis, CDN, and related tools with configuration guidance.

faq.question: Is the database cleanup guidance safe for production?
faq.answer: Only with backups, staging validation, and careful review. Some examples delete data or optimize live tables.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace a hosting or CDN expert?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure performance work, but hosting, CDN, and plugin choices still need site-specific testing.
